findings.headline: Dynagas linked to $1bn Samsung LNG quartet
findings.note: One day before the strict Sept 17 window start; included because it was surfaced by the in-window Ring C sweep and is a genuinely new, sizeable cluster with no existing backend match. Samsung Heavy Industries disclosed (per its own DART filing, relayed by Splash) a contract with an 'unidentified Oceania-based owner' on Monday 2026-09-14: four 200,000 cbm LNG carriers, ~KRW1.41trn (~$1.05bn), delivery by September 2029. Splash's headline links the order to Dynagas (George Procopiou) as an inference from Procopiou's wider group newbuilding push -- Dynagas is NOT named as the confirmed owner in the article body; the confirmed fact is only 'unidentified Oceania-based owner.' Backend already carries 16 Dynagas-owned vessels (Yamal LNG Arc7 icebreakers and 'Clean'-series US LNG carriers, all at HD Hyundai HI / Hanwha Ocean) but none at Samsung Heavy Industries, so a Samsung cluster would be new to Dynagas's backend footprint if confirmed. NOT added as a candidate -- owner is unconfirmed and Rule F / no-value-without-ref bars proposing 'Dynagas' as Shipowner on an inference. Flagged to backend_findings for a future pass once the owner is confirmed (DART original filing or a follow-up article naming the buyer).

findings.headline: Exmar lands 10-year Abidjan FSRU deal
findings.note: Exmar signed a 10-year floating LNG infrastructure deal with Ivory Coast's CI-Energies and Petroci reviving a decade-old Abidjan import-terminal plan; covers lease of a 152,000 cbm FSRU. No specific vessel/hull is named in the article -- reads as a terminal/charter deployment story, not a newbuild order, and backend currently has zero Exmar-owned FSRU rows at all (checked: no Exmar + Vessel type=FSRU match). Not enough to build a candidate row (no vessel name/IMO/hull -- would violate 'never fabricate'). Flagged to backend_findings: watch for the specific FSRU Exmar assigns to Abidjan, and separately worth a look at why Exmar has zero FSRU rows in the backend at all (may be a genuine existing-fleet gap, better suited to the FSRU reconciliation SOP).

(1) The MOL/NYK ownership plus the 9/8 HD Hyundai-group / Samsung HI builder split matches what a July 2026 imarinenews article reported (read earlier in this session, before compaction; I was unable to relocate the exact URL afresh in this continuation -- imarinenews's own site search returned no results for repeated query attempts, and WebSearch is exhausted, so this citation needs to be re-sourced by a follow-on session rather than asserted from memory). (2) A real discrepancy worth flagging: the backend's builder vocabulary distinguishes 'HD Hyundai Samho' from 'HD Hyundai Heavy Industries' as separate controlled values elsewhere in the sheet (confirmed: both values are in active use), but rows 1184-1192 use the generic 'HD Hyundai Heavy Industries' label. If the underlying press specifically named the Samho yard (as the task brief states), the backend's builder value on those 9 rows may need correcting to 'HD Hyundai Samho' -- but this needs a fresh, re-verified source before proposing it as a fix, per the §3.8 gate. (3) No post-July, post-deadline (September 2026) update was found on whether the reservation converted to firm contracts, lapsed, or is still pending -- Woodside/Mozambique-specific newsroom and category-page fetches did not surface anything newer, and this is exactly the kind of query WebSearch would normally answer.
